3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: It felt like eternity since the Benfi Festival. Had it really only been less than 24 hours?

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: I was at home now, drinking an afternoon coffee on my balcony. A stack of newspapers lay by my side. I picked them up one by one, reading and re-reading the articles about the festival.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: I started regretting my decisions. Regardless, it was too late now. The damage was done.

35.speaker: Monica
35.text: "All I wanted was to bring the people of Sordland together, the way you're able to. But not like this."

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: Her eyes were getting moist. A single tear fell onto the newsprint.

39.speaker: Player
39.text: “If you are going to succeed in this, you have to be stronger. I know you can be.”

40.speaker: Player
40.text: “I did warn you. But you were always stubborn.”

42.speaker: Monica
42.text: “I know. I'm sorry. But you are right.”

43.speaker: Narrator
43.text: Her eyes filled with gratitude. I could see she'd slept as little as I had since the festival.

46.speaker: Monica
46.text: “One more thing. You know how stubborn I am.”

48.speaker: Player
48.text: "Monica, I know. We can talk about this--”

51.speaker: Monica
51.text: “What is there to talk about? I'm a disgrace with no support from my husband. It says so right here.”

52.speaker: Monica
52.text: “Here, I have it memorized: First Lady disgraced. No support from her husband.”

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: She grabbed one of the newspapers from the top of the stack and started reading out what a columnist wrote.

56.speaker: Monica
56.text: “With her shameful outburst at Anrica mayor Curtan Leste, First Lady Monica Rayne once again proved that politics is an area best left to gentlemen."

58.speaker: Monica
58.text: “You can't even stand Leste, and you took his side! While making me look like a fool!”

59.speaker: Narrator
59.text: She started ripping the newspaper to shreds.

60.speaker: Monica
60.text: “After all these years by your side, playing the doting wife...”

61.speaker: Monica
61.text: “You know... my mother was right about you.”

62.speaker: Player
62.text: “Darling, believe me. My hands were tied.”

64.speaker: Player
64.text: “I'm so sorry. I understand if you never forgive me.”

65.speaker: Player
65.text: “I thought you were capable of defending yourself. Clearly not.”

66.speaker: Monica
66.text: “Just...tell me why. Couldn't you have said something?"

67.speaker: Player
67.text: “I didn't want to lose Curtan's support.”

69.speaker: Monica
69.text: “No, no. No you didn't. How is this even legal?"

77.speaker: Player
77.text: “I have to tell you something. I made a deal with Curtan.”

85.speaker: Player
85.text: “Sometimes you have to make sacrifices for the good of the country. You've got to learn that if you want to enter politics.”

86.speaker: Monica
86.text: “But why did the sacrifice have to be me? Never mind. You had your reasons."

87.speaker: Player
87.text: “I'll give you one more chance. But this time I won't tolerate it if it meddles with how I run the country.”

88.speaker: Player
88.text: “You always have my support. I failed you this time -- it won't happen again."

89.speaker: Monica
89.text: “I-- I can live with that, I suppose.”

91.speaker: Player
91.text: “No. I was right not to let you speak at the festival. Next time, I won't bring you at all."

97.speaker: Monica
97.text: “I-- I suppose I can appreciate that.”

98.speaker: Monica

321.speaker: Monica
321.text: "When I gave that speech, I saw hope in the eyes of all the women in the audience. This is the right path for me, Anton."

325.speaker: Monica
325.text: "I know this isn't an urgent issue for you. But it's vital to me."

326.speaker: Monica
326.text: "I know this is something you're passionate about as well. Can I count on you?"

331.speaker: Monica
331.text: "Oh, Anton. This means so much to me!"

332.speaker: Narrator
332.text: Monica hugged me tightly, and I felt some of the past day's tension melt away.

333.speaker: Narrator
333.text: Monica gave me a quick hug.

339.speaker: Player_Italic
339.text: Gesture for her to sit down.

343.speaker: Narrator
343.text: Monica sat and picked up the nearest newspaper. She pointed to a particularly insulting headline on the front page.

344.speaker: Narrator
344.text: Monica sat and picked up the nearest newspaper. She flipped it open to the article about Curtan's apology.

345.speaker: Monica
345.text: "I've been reading the papers, too. I'm happy the confrontation with Curtan didn't seem to have caused much damage. But it could have gone so much worse."

346.speaker: Monica
346.text: “I'm glad that beast admitted he was in the wrong. But it could very easily have gone another way.”

347.speaker: Monica
347.text: “I never in a million years would have wished for this, Anton.”

348.speaker: Player
348.text: “It's okay. I've had Curtan fired. That's the last of our troubles with him."

395.speaker: Monica
395.text: "You were right. Gloria was right. I made myself look like an idiot and damaged the very cause I was fighting for."

398.speaker: Monica
398.text: “With the President providing no support, her challenge to Leste was quickly defeated."

399.speaker: Monica
399.text: “Powerless to defend herself from this challenge, she turned to the President, who provided no support."
